# Enable API gateway for Kubernetes

The Consul API gateway ships with Consul and is automatically installed when you install Consul on Kubernetes. Before you begin the installation process, verify that the environment you are deploying Consul and the API gateway in meets the requirements listed in the [Technical Specifications](/consul/docs/north-south/api-gateway/k8s/tech-specs). Refer to the [Release Notes](/consul/docs/release-notes) for any additional information about the version you are deploying.

1. The Consul Helm chart deploys the API gateway using the configuration specified in the `values.yaml` file. Refer to [Helm Chart Configuration - `connectInject.apiGateway`](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/helm#apigateway) for information about the Helm chart configuration options. Create a `values.yaml` file for configuring your Consul API gateway deployment and include the following settings:

  <Tabs>

    <Tab heading="Reference configuration">
    <CodeBlockConfig filename="values.yaml">

    ```yaml
    global:
      name: consul
    connectInject:
      enabled: true
      apiGateway:
        manageExternalCRDs: true
    ```

    </CodeBlockConfig>
    </Tab>

    <Tab heading="OpenShift">

    If you are installing Consul on an OpenShift Kubernetes cluster, you must include the `global.openShift.enabled` parameter and set it to `true`. Refer to [OpenShift requirements](/consul/docs/connect/gateways/api-gateway/tech-specs#openshift-requirements) for additional information.

    <CodeBlockConfig filename="values.yaml">

     ```yaml
     global:
       openshift:
         enabled: true
     connectInject:
       enabled: true
       apiGateway:
         manageExternalCRDs: true
       cni:
         enabled: true
         logLevel: info
         multus: true
         cniBinDir: "/var/lib/cni/bin"
         cniNetDir: "/etc/kubernetes/cni/net.d"
     ```
    </CodeBlockConfig>
    </Tab>

    <Tab heading="GKE Autopilot">

    By default, GKE Autopilot installs [Gateway API resources](https://gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io), so we recommend customizing the `connectInject.apiGateway` stanza to accommodate the pre-installed Gateway API CRDs.

    The following working example enables both Consul Service Mesh and Consul API Gateway on GKE Autopilot. Refer to [`connectInject.agiGateway` in the Helm chart reference](https://developer.hashicorp.com/consul/docs/reference/k8s/helm#v-connectinject-apigateway) for additional information.

    <CodeBlockConfig filename="values.yaml">

     ```yaml
     global:
       name: consul
     connectInject:
       enabled: true
       apiGateway:
         manageExternalCRDs: false
         manageNonStandardCRDs: true
       cni:
         enabled: true
         logLevel: debug
         cniBinDir: "/home/kubernetes/bin"
         cniNetDir: "/etc/cni/net.d"
     server:
       resources:
         requests:
           memory: "500Mi"
           cpu: "500m"
         limits:
           memory: "500Mi"
           cpu: "500m"
     ```
    </CodeBlockConfig>
    </Tab>

  </Tabs>

1. Install Consul API Gateway using the standard Consul Helm chart or Consul K8s CLI specify the custom values file. Refer to the [Consul Helm chart](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul-k8s/releases) in GitHub releases for the available versions.

  <Tabs>
  <Tab heading="Consul K8s CLI (Mac Only)">
  
  Refer to the official [Consul K8S CLI documentation](/consul/docs/reference/cli/consul-k8s) to find additional settings.
  
  ```shell-session
  $ brew tap hashicorp/tap
  ```
  
  ```shell-session
  $ brew install hashicorp/tap/consul-k8s
  ```
  
  ```shell-session
  $ consul-k8s install -config-file=values.yaml -set global.image=hashicorp/consul:1.17.0
  ```
  
  </Tab>
  <Tab heading="Helm">
  
  Add the HashiCorp Helm repository.
  
  ```shell-session
  $ helm repo add hashicorp https://helm.releases.hashicorp.com
  ```
  
  Install Consul with API Gateway on your Kubernetes cluster by specifying the `values.yaml` file.
  
  ```shell-session
  $ helm install consul hashicorp/consul --version 1.3.0 --values values.yaml --create-namespace --namespace consul
  ```
  
  </Tab>
  </Tabs>


## Configure additional gateway classes for independent scaling

By default, the Consul Helm chart creates one `GatewayClass` named `consul` and one `GatewayClassConfig` named `consul-api-gateway`. Every `Gateway` resource that does not explicitly override `spec.gatewayClassName` uses this default `consul` class, which means all gateways in the cluster share the same replica count, resource requests/limits, and other deployment settings.

If you need different scaling or resource settings for different gateways, such as giving one application's gateway more CPU and replicas than another's, you can create additional `GatewayClass` and `GatewayClassConfig` pairs and assign them to specific `Gateway` resources.

### How gateway classes and gateway class configs relate

The following objects work together to determine how a gateway is deployed:

| Object | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`Gateway`](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/api-gateway/gateway) | Declares the gateway and its listeners. Its `spec.gatewayClassName` field selects which `GatewayClass` to use. |
| [`GatewayClass`](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/api-gateway/gatewayclass) | A template for gateways. Its `spec.controllerName` field determines which Consul controller manages gateways created from this class, and its `spec.parametersRef` field points to a `GatewayClassConfig`. |
| [`GatewayClassConfig`](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/api-gateway/gatewayclassconfig) | Specifies the actual deployment settings for gateways, such as replica counts, CPU/memory resources, and service type. |

A `Gateway` references a `GatewayClass` by name, and that `GatewayClass` references a `GatewayClassConfig` by name through `parametersRef`. Because `GatewayClass` and `GatewayClassConfig` are both cluster-scoped resources, you can define as many pairs as you need and reuse them across `Gateway` resources in any namespace.

### Create a custom gateway class and gateway class config

1. Create a `GatewayClassConfig` that defines the deployment settings you want for this group of gateways.

   <CodeBlockConfig filename="gatewayclassconfig-app1.yaml">

   ```yaml
   apiVersion: consul.hashicorp.com/v1alpha1
   kind: GatewayClassConfig
   metadata:
     name: consul-api-gateway-app1
   spec:
     deployment:
       defaultInstances: 2
       minInstances: 1
       maxInstances: 4
     resources:
       requests:
         cpu: 200m
         memory: 200Mi
       limits:
         cpu: 200m
         memory: 200Mi
     serviceType: LoadBalancer
   ```

   </CodeBlockConfig>

1. Create a `GatewayClass` that references the `GatewayClassConfig` you created. Set `spec.controllerName` to match the edition of API gateway you are running:

   - Use `consul.hashicorp.com/gateway-controller` for the standard (stable) API gateway. This controller runs by default.
   - Use `consul.hashicorp.com/gateway-controller-consul` for the Consul API gateway. This controller only runs when you install the Consul API gateway CRDs by setting `global.crds.consulapi.enabled` to `true` in your Helm values. If this controller is not running, any `GatewayClass` that references it is not reconciled and its gateways are never deployed.

   <CodeBlockConfig filename="gatewayclass-app1.yaml">

   ```yaml
   apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
   kind: GatewayClass
   metadata:
     name: consul-app1
   spec:
     controllerName: consul.hashicorp.com/gateway-controller
     parametersRef:
       group: consul.hashicorp.com
       kind: GatewayClassConfig
       name: consul-api-gateway-app1
   ```

   </CodeBlockConfig>

1. Apply both configurations to your cluster.

   ```shell-session
   $ kubectl apply -f gatewayclassconfig-app1.yaml
   $ kubectl apply -f gatewayclass-app1.yaml
   ```

1. Reference the new `GatewayClass` from any `Gateway` resource by setting `spec.gatewayClassName`. Gateways that omit this field, or that set it to `consul`, continue to use the default class and share the chart's default settings.

   <CodeBlockConfig filename="gateway-app1.yaml">

   ```yaml
   apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1beta1
   kind: Gateway
   metadata:
     name: api-gateway-app1
     namespace: app1
     labels:
       component: api-gateway
   spec:
     gatewayClassName: consul-app1
     listeners:
       - protocol: HTTP
         port: 80
         name: http
         allowedRoutes:
           namespaces:
             from: All
       - protocol: TCP
         port: 8090
         name: tcp-8090
         allowedRoutes:
           namespaces:
             from: All
   ```

   </CodeBlockConfig>

Repeat these steps to create additional `GatewayClass`/`GatewayClassConfig` pairs for other applications or teams. Each pair can define its own replica counts and resource requests independently of the default gateway class, so that individual gateways can be scaled or resourced according to their own workload requirements without affecting the shared default configuration.
